See also {{cog|nl|-}} and {{cog|sv|hand|t=hand}}, {{cog|da|hånd}}, {{cog|de|Hand}}, {{cog|fy|hân}}. Perhaps compare Old Swedish {{m|sv|hinna||to gain}}, {{cog|got|𐍆𐍂𐌰𐌷𐌹𐌽𐌸𐌰𐌽|𐍆𐍂𐌰-𐌷𐌹𐌽𐌸𐌰𐌽|to take captive, capture}}; and {{cog|lv|sīts||hunting spear}}, {{cog|grc|κεντέω||prick}}, {{cog|sq|çandër||pitchfork, prop}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # The [[part]] of the [[forelimb]] below the [[forearm]] or [[wrist]] in humans and other [[primate|primates]], and the corresponding part in many other [[animal]]s. #: {{meronyms|en|index finger|middle finger|palm|pinky|ring finger|thumb}} #: {{ux|en|Her '''hands''' are really strong.}} #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=7|passage=I made a speaking trumpet of my '''hands''' and commenced to whoop “Ahoy!” and “Hello!” at the top of my lungs. {{...}} The Colonel woke up, and, after asking what in brimstone was the matter, opened his mouth and roared “Hi!” and “Hello!” like the bull of Bashan.}} #* {{RQ:NYT|date=26 December 2012|author=[[w:John Branch (journalist)|John Branch]]|title=Snow Fall: The Avalanche at Tunnel Creek|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114133825/http://www.nytimes.com/projects/2012/snow-fall/?smid=fb-nytimes&WT.z_sma=SP_SNT_20130415#/?part=tunnel-creek|passage=Using her '''hands''' like windshield wipers, she tried to flick snow away from her mouth. When she clawed at her chest and neck, the crumbs maddeningly slid back onto her face. She grew claustrophobic.}} # ''That which resembles, or to some extent performs the office of, a human hand.'' ## A limb of certain animals, such as the [[foot]] of a hawk, or any one of the four extremities of a monkey. ## An index or [[pointer]] on a dial; such as the hour and minute hands on the [[face]] of an analog [[clock]], which are used to indicate the [[time]] of day. # ''That which is, or may be, held in a hand at once.'' ## {{senseid|en|card games}} {{lb|en|card games}} The set of [[card]]s held by a player. ### {{lb|en|mahjong}} The set of [[tile]]s held by a player. ### A [[round]] of a card game. ## {{lb|en|tobacco manufacturing}} A bundle of tobacco leaves tied together. ## {{senseid|en|bunch}} {{lb|en|collective}} A bunch of [[bananas]], a typical retail amount, where individual fruits are [[finger]]s. # {{senseid|en|measurement}} ''In linear measurement:'' ## {{lb|en|chiefly|in measuring the [[height]] of [[horse]]s}} Four [[inch]]es, a hand's [[breadth]]. ##* {{RQ:Orwell Animal Farm|I|6|passage=Boxer was an enormous beast, nearly eighteen '''hands''' high, and as strong as any two ordinary horses put together.}} ## {{lb|en|obsolete}} Three [[inch]]es. # A [[side]]; part, camp; direction, either right or left. #* {{RQ:KJV|Exodus|38|15|page=180|column=1|passage={{...}}on this '''hand''' and that '''hand''' ''were'' hangings{{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Milton Eikonoklastes|chapter=Upon the Rebellion in Ireland|page=125|passage=For that the Proteſtants were then on the winning '''hand''', it muſt needs be plain; who notwithſtanding the miſs of thoſe Forces which, at thir landing heer, maiſter’d without difficulty great part of Wales and Cheſhire, yet made a ſhift to keep thir ownw in ''Ireland''.}} # Power of performance; means of execution; ability; skill; dexterity. #* {{RQ:Spectator|author=Addison|volume=V|issue=499|date=2 October 1712|page=451|passage=My friend Will Honeycomb has told me, for above this half year, that he had a great mind to try his '''hand''' at a Spectator, and that he would fain have one of his writing in my works.}} #* {{RQ:Rinehart Hopwood Bat|The Shadow of the Bat|6|The Bat—they called him the Bat.{{nb...}}. He'd never been in stir, the bulls had never mugged him, he didn't run with a mob, he played a lone '''hand''', and fenced his stuff so that even the Fence couldn't swear he knew his face.}} # {{lb|en|especially in compounds}} An [[agent]]; a [[servant]], or manual laborer; a [[workman]], trained or competent for special service or duty. #: {{ux|en|Large farms need many farm '''hands'''.}} #* {{RQ:Locke Human Understanding|chapter=|section=|page=259|passage=But a Dictionary of this ſort, containing, as it were, a Natural Hiſtory, requires too many '''hands''', as well as too much time, coſt, pains, and ſagacity, ever to be hoped for; and till that be done, we muſt content our ſelves with ſuch Definitions of the Names of Subſtances, as explain the ſenſe Men uſe them in.}} #* {{RQ:Orczy Miss Elliott|chapter=The Affair at the Novelty Theatre|passage=For this scene, a large number of supers are engaged, and in order to further swell the crowd, practically all the available stage '''hands''' have to ‘walk on’ dressed in various coloured dominoes, and all wearing masks.}} # A performer more or less skilful. #: {{ux|en|an old '''hand''' at public speaking}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1903|author=George Horace Lorimer|title=Letters from a Self-Made Merchant to his Son|page=46 |passage=At the church sociables he used to hop around among them, chipping and chirping like a dicky-bird picking up seed; and he was a great '''hand''' to play the piano, and sing saddish, sweetish songs to them.}} # An instance of [[help]]ing. #: {{ux|en|Bob gave Alice a '''hand''' to move the furniture.}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis||passage=What need have you of a '''hand''' who never fall?|46}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=58|passage=The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no '''hand''' in the furnishing of that atrocious house.}} # {{U|handwriting}}; style of [[penmanship]]. #: {{ux|en|a good '''hand'''}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|IV|iii|202|2|I ſay ſhe neuer did inuent this letter, / This is a mans inuention, and his '''hand'''.}} #* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|volume=IV|book=X|chapter=Containing Instructions Very Necessary to Be Perused by Modern Critics|page=4|passage={{...}}I have ſometimes known a Poet in Danger of being convicted as a Thief, upon much worſe Evidence than the Reſemblance of '''Hands''' hath been held to be in the Law.}} #* {{RQ:Stevenson Treasure Island|chapter=The Sea Chest|page=31|passage={{...}}I found written on the other side, in a very good, clear '''hand''', this short message{{nb...}}}} #* {{RQ:Stevenson Jekyll and Hyde|pages=74–75|pageref=74|passage='This is a strange note,' said Mr. Utterson; and then sharply, 'How do you come to have it open?' 'The man at Maw's was main angry, sir, and he threw it back to me like so much dirt,' returned Poole. 'This is unquestionably the doctor's '''hand''', do you know?' resumed the lawyer. 'I thought it looked like it,' said the servant rather sulkily; and then, with another voice, 'But what matters '''hand''' of write,' he said. 'I've seen him!'}} #* {{quote-journal|en|author=Jane Shilling|title=The Golden Thread: the Story of Writing, by Ewan Clayton, review [print edition: Illuminating language]|url=http://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/books/historybookreviews/10304108/The-Golden-Thread-the-Story-of-Writing-by-Ewan-Clayton-review.html| work={{w|The Daily Telegraph}} (Review)| date=14 September 2013| page=R28| passage=[T]he pleasure of writing on wax with a stylus is exemplified by the fine, flowing '''hand''' of a Roman scribe who made out the birth certificate of Herennia Gemella, born March 128 AD.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250711011038/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/books/historybookreviews/10304108/The-Golden-Thread-the-Story-of-Writing-by-Ewan-Clayton-review.html|archivedate=11 July 2025}} # A person's autograph or signature. #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=ii|page=21|passage=Who {{...}} Haue paſt the armie of the mightie Turke:
Bearing his priuie ſignet and his '''hand''',
To ſafe conduct vs thorow ''Affrica'': {{...}}}} #: {{ux|en|Given under my '''Hand''' and Seal of the State this 1st Day of January, 2010.}} # [[promise|Promise]], [[word]]; especially of a [[betrothal]]. #*: They once made Mourning and Fasting for the Death of the ''English'' Governor, who had given his '''Hand''' to come on such a Day to 'em, and neither came nor sent; believing, when a Man's Word was past, nothing but Death could or should prevent his keeping it: And when they saw he was not dead, they ask'd him what Name they had for a Man who promis'd a Thing he did not do? #* {{quote-book|en|year=1868|author=William Carleton|title=Traits and Stories of the Irish Peasantry|volume=2|page=179 |passage=Few would rely upon the word or oath of any man who had been known to break a '''hand'''-promise.}} # Personal possession; ownership. #* {{RQ:Knolles Turkes |passage=Receiving in '''hand''' one year’s tribute.}} # {{lb|en|chiefly|in the plural}} [[management|Management]], [[domain]], [[control]]. #: {{ux|en|in safe '''hands'''}} #: {{ux|en|in good '''hands'''}} #: {{ux|en|With the business back in the founder's '''hands''', there is new hope for the company.}} #: {{ux|en|With John in charge of the project, it's in good '''hands'''.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|Luke|1|1|page=1279|column=1|passage=Foraſmuch as many haue taken in '''hande''' to ſet foorth in order a declaration of thoſe things which are moſt ſurely beleeued among vs{{nb...}}}} #* {{RQ:Bacon Baconiana|page=21|passage=It is my purpoſe to give a true and plain Account, of the Deſigns and Labours of a very great Philoſopher amongſt us; and to offer to the World, in ſome tollerable Method, thoſe ''Remains'' of his, which to that end, were put into my '''Hands'''.}} #* {{RQ:Milton History|page=81|passage=But ''Albinus'' in thoſe troubleſome times enſuing under the ſhort reign of ''Pertinax'' and ''Didius Julianus'', found means to keep in his '''hands''' the Government of ''Britain'';}} # {{lb|en|colloquial|negative polarity plural}} A hand which is free to [[assist]]; especially due to having one's hands [[full]] or otherwise fully [[preoccupied]]. #: {{ux|en|Just give me a minute — I haven't got any '''hands''' right now.}} # [[applause|Applause]]. #: {{ux|en|[[give someone a hand|Give him a '''hand''']].}} #* {{RQ:Thackeray Pendennis||passage=“Give him a '''hand''', Pendennis; you know every chap likes a '''hand''',” Mr. Foker said; and the good-natured young gentleman, and Pendennis laughing, and the dragoons in the opposite box, began clapping hands to the best of their power.|3}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=11 January 2013|author=Tom Shone|journal=The Guardian|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/film/filmblog/2013/jan/11/oscar-nominations-surprise-taste |passage=Also a big '''hand''' for Silver Linings Playbook, an exuberant modern screwball comedy we had, in an unseemly fit of cynicism, deemed "too entertaining" for Academy voters.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013141000/https://www.theguardian.com/film/filmblog/2013/jan/11/oscar-nominations-surprise-taste|archivedate=13 October 2026}} # {{lb|en|historical}} A [[Native American]] [[gambling]] [[game]], involving guessing the whereabouts of bits of [[ivory]] or similar, which are passed rapidly from hand to hand. # {{lb|en|firearms}} The small part of a [[gunstock]] near the lock, which is grasped by the hand in taking aim. # A whole [[rhizome]] of [[ginger]]. # The [[feel]] of a [[fabric]]; the [[impression]] or [[quality]] of the fabric as judged qualitatively by the sense of [[touch]]. #: {{ux|en|This fabric has a smooth, soft '''hand'''.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|journal=Handwoven|year=2026|volume=XLVII|number=1|page=64|title=Jeweled Beetle Runner|author=Rahul Kiran K. |text=He finds that this double beat helps lock the weft in place and gives the cloth a sturdy, durable '''hand''', perfect for a functional piece such as a runner.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} Actual performance; deed; act; workmanship; agency; hence, manner of performance. #* {{RQ:KJV|Judges|6|36|page=345|column=1|passage=And Gideon ſaid vnto God, If thou wilt ſaue Iſrael by mine '''hand''',{{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Clarendon History|book=VIII|page=605|passage=They who thought they could never be ſecure in any Peace, except the King were firſt at their Mercy, and ſo obliged to accept the conditions they would give him, were willing to change the '''hand''' in carrying on the War: and many, who thought the Earl of ''Eſſex'' behaved himſelf too imperiouſly, were willing to have the Command in one who was more their equal.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} Agency in transmission from one person to another. #: {{ux|en|to buy at first '''hand''' (from the producer, or when new)}} #: {{ux|en|to buy at second '''hand''' (when no longer in the producer’s hand, or when not new)}} #: {{ux|en|It's not a rumor. I heard it at first '''hand'''.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} Rate; price. #* {{RQ:Bacon Essayes|chapter=Of Dispatch. XXV.|page=143|passage=For Time is the meaſure of Buſineſſe, as Money is of Wares: And Buſineſſe is bought at a deare '''Hand''', where there is ſmall ''diſpatch''.}} # {{lb|en|slang|in the plural|with "got"}} An unexpected strength or ability to cause someone trouble. #: {{ux|en|Damn, this flu shot got '''hands'''.}} =====Usage notes===== * The word ''hand'' is used figuratively for a large variety of acts or objects, in the doing, or making, or use of which the hand is in some way employed or concerned; also, as a symbol to denote various qualities or conditions, as, : (a) Activity; operation; work; — in distinction from the [[head]], which implies thought, and the [[heart]], which implies affection. :: His '''hand''' will be against every man. — ''Genesis 16:12'' : (b) Power; might; supremacy; — often in the Scriptures. :: With a mighty '''hand''' . . . will I rule over you. — ''Ezekiel 20:33''. : (c) Fraternal feeling; for example ''to give, or take, the '''hand'''; to give the right '''hand''''' : (d) Contract; — commonly of marriage; for example ''to ask the '''hand'''; to pledge the '''hand''''' =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|part of the arm below the wrist}} {{l|en|manus}}
